summary: The last Forest Service lookout remaining in Nevada, a 1931-32 4AR cab above Lake Tahoe now on private land, leased for cell antennas since 1997 and once proposed for a move to White Hill.

facts.design: 4AR-style enclosed cab, one of twelve surviving nationwide
facts.status_note: Standing as of the sources checked (2001 and 2013 reporting); a 2013 USFS proposal to dismantle and relocate it to White Hill above Spooner Summit was not confirmed as carried out or abandoned.

access.note: Sits on a 1.1-acre private parcel owned by Zephyr Cove Properties; the Forest Service holds only a right-of-way easement. Not open to public visitation at this site as of the sources checked.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (historic administrator; land now privately owned)

events.note: Construction began winter 1931, funded partly by local supporter A. K. Bourne ($1,500) and Douglas County (road access). The National Historic Lookout Register gives the completed build year as 1932.

U.S. Forest Service staffing ended in 1954 when the Nevada Division of Forestry took over operation. The tower closed for the season in October 1964 and continued in use afterward; one source describes it as the last lookout NDF still operated in western Nevada, into the 1970s.

Listed on the National Historic Lookout Register October 8, 1998, as US 278 / NV 1; nominated by Mark Swift. Found NRHP-eligible in 1997 (a separate, earlier determination reported only by the South Tahoe Now article).

corrections.evidence: Tahoe Daily Tribune reports the tower sits on a 1.1-acre parcel owned by Zephyr Cove Properties, with the Forest Service holding only a right-of-way easement for access; Pacific Bell Wireless has leased the structure since 1997.

sources.title: Zephyr Cove lookout seen as historical
Forest Service proposes to relocate Zephyr Point Lookout

notes_for_editor: Source [2] (westlookouts.weebly.com) is an amateur compilation site, apparently drawn from old newspaper clippings; its specific names (Buck Wheeler, Jim Cain, A.K. Bourne, Mrs. T.C. Clifton) and fire dates (1936, 1941) could not be cross-checked against a primary source and should be verified against Nevada newspaper archives if this page gets more scrutiny. The build year (1931 start vs. NHLR's 1932 completion) is not a real conflict - both describe the same winter 1931-32 construction. On fact-checking, the 1964/1970 staffing detail was also not a real cross-source conflict: 'closed for the season' in 1964 (source 2) describes a routine seasonal closure, not an end date, and source 3 (Tahoe Daily Tribune) independently corroborates staffing continuing into the 1970s - the story previously framed this as 'sources disagree,' which overstated it, and has been corrected. Also corrected on fact-check: the NRHP-eligibility-in-1997 claim was mis-cited to sources 1/3, which don't contain it; it is only in source 4 (South Tahoe Now), and has been re-cited there. The source 3 article (Tahoe Daily Tribune) is itself dated December 19, 2001, not current - it names a 'National Trust for Historic Preservation' registry listing, a different, private-nonprofit designation from NRHP eligibility; the story does not currently mention that National Trust listing. 'Last Forest Service lookout built in the state' was also corrected to 'remaining in the state,' since NHLR's source text says 'the last U.S. Forest Service lookout in Nevada' (i.e., the only one left), not that it was the last one constructed. The 2013 relocation-to-White-Hill proposal's outcome is unknown; could not find any later source confirming or denying the move happened, so current physical location/status is uncertain despite the tower record's 'standing' status. A 2001 Las Vegas Sun piece and a 2013 Carson Now piece look relevant but returned paywall/403 errors and were not used.
